E1.title: House of Spirits
E1.text: House of Spirits may refer to:

E2.title: The House of the Spirits
E2.text: The novel has also been adapted for the theater in a version written by Caridad Svich, which was commissioned by Repertorio Espanol in New York City.

E3.title: The House of the Spirits
E3.text: That adaptation premiered in 2009 and received the HOLA Award for Outstanding Achievement in Playwriting from the Hispanic Organization of Latin Actors.

E4.title: The House of the Spirits
E4.text: Unlike the film and the previous adaptation, this version was written and performed in Spanish and has been staged in Latin American countries such as Chile and Costa Rica.

E5.title: The House of the Spirits
E5.text: Svich also wrote an English language version of the play which won the 2011 American Theatre Critics Association Primus Prize for its production at Denver Center Theatre Company in 2010.

E6.title: The House of the Spirits
E6.text: In 1993, the book was adapted into a film by Danish director Bille August.

E7.title: The House of the Spirits
E7.text: The movie starred Jeremy Irons as Esteban Trueba, Meryl Streep as Clara del Valle Trueba, Winona Ryder as Blanca Trueba, Glenn Close as Férula Trueba and Antonio Banderas as Pedro Tercero García.

E8.title: The House of the Spirits
E8.text: While the film won some minor international awards, it was widely viewed as a critical failure.

E9.title: The House of the Spirits

E40.text: In January 8, 1981, I was living in Venezuela and I received a phone call that my beloved grandfather was dying.
